data.standardized_narrative: At 31 December 2023 the syndicate's gross claims outstanding opening balance was 598.6 (USD millions). Analysis of the gross claims development triangle shows net favourable prior-year development of approximately 38.7 (USD millions) (a ~6.5% release relative to opening gross claims). The release was driven by favourable claims development primarily on the 2020 and 2021 underwriting years (2020 favourable development specifically quantified as $17.8m). Named US catastrophe events (eg. Hurricane Ian, Winter Storm Uri, Hurricane Ida) materially impacted earlier years, but 2023 development benefitted from lower severity of catastrophe events and favourable run-off.
raw_causal_phrases: The 2020 year of account has produced a net profit of $20.1m, inclusive of favourable claims development during the 2023 calendar year of $17.8m.
After the first three years of the Syndicate being impacted by US catastrophes, the 2023 loss ratio is an improvement on the prior year and reflects the underwriting actions taken on the portfolio.

The current year catastrophe claims ratio is 9.4% which has reduced from 17.5% in 2022, albeit the current year includes a higher frequency of convective and winter storms. The current year benefitted from a lower severity of catastrophe events, Hurricane Ian contributed 12.8pts to the equivalent 2022 ratio.
The total estimate for insurance losses incurred but not reported at 31 December 2023 is $384.3m (2022: $414.4m).
data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development (38.7) was calculated from the gross claims development triangle (note 13) by comparing current estimates to the prior diagonal for underwriting years 2020 and 2021 (excluding 2022 and 2023 per methodology). No explicit single-line 'Movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' gross total was found; the triangle was used as the authoritative gross source. All amounts are in the report's native currency (USD millions). Some LOB-level prior year movements are not quantified by the report and are inferred at low confidence.
